decision: Needs Fixes: raw adapter overhead reduced; end-to-end performance preservation and supported-hardware validation are not established
notes: Complete imported main85, preceding opt9 and current dense3 production Python; --lookup default; no prototype or runtime monkeypatch in timings.
Raw: GPU 1 / CPU affinity 4-7; two-rank pipelines: GPUs 1,2 / affinity 4-11. Shared PCIe Blackwell host, no NVLink or physical multi-node test.
128 features, batch 32, hotness 4, D=64, FP32/SGD; resident repeated keys, 20 warmups, six trials of 100 steps, five separately profiled steps.
Each six-process workload uses main,old,dense,dense,old,main order; the additional SparseDist reverse control uses dense,old,old,dense. Preserve all samples and outliers.
No other local GPU validation ran during these timed processes; external jobs and host scheduling still vary. End-to-end timings do not establish parity or a stable improvement.
Target stack: torch2.13/cu130, TorchRec1.8.0+0ea0ec0, FBGEMM1.8/cu130, NCCL2.30.7 headers/extension/preload with Torch2.29.7 dependency; not a certified single-NCCL NGC container.
Older stack: torch2.7/cu128, TorchRec/FBGEMM1.2, NCCL2.28.9 preload, no hierarchical ops; two-rank tests disable P2P/IB and use loopback.

No C++ or optimizer-format changes in this follow-up. Training extension/fatbin builds are the matching main85 plus publication refinement documented in input_dist_optimization_results.json; inference bindings disabled.
Dense3 production Python digest is 6cf177ccde3e6416c7eb7ab284a2bc606c9db6931bd86f20d5b65822f3f7d44b. Later test-only changes warm the initialization operator and add six half-cancellation cases.

Negative controls are separate staged runtime copies, not production changes. Removing record_stream fails; removing ready wait first passed due to lazy loading, then fails after exact-op warmup; normal warmed test passes.
Initial dense1 failure was a test fixture torch.full size argument, corrected before dense2; it is not a production-path defect.

notes: Current implementation is pool2: bounded per-distributor idle entries with static dist_init and a weak resolver cell. Pool1/classmethod variants and the global-pool prototype are unpublished experiments, retained as historical diagnostics.

At most eight idle entries are cached per distributor, not an in-flight request limit. Native/fused awaitables own source KJTs. Returning an entry clears its weak cell; cache copies/unpickling start empty.

Production Python changes only shard/input_dist.py relative to e778622. No C++/optimizer/raw-table/dense-kernel changes. Runtime deltas below reconstruct exact manifests from the already recorded parent manifests.

Target/older receiver+lifecycle matrices use final production source but precede added weak-result and distinct-active-type assertions. Final contract matrices rerun the result checks; final one-case burst tests rerun all strengthened checks on both stacks. Production Python stays identical.
The previous e778622 full table suite and 297-case dense suite remain bounded evidence for unchanged raw-table/dense code; they were not rerun in this controller-only follow-up.

CPU attribution uses perf_counter_ns wrappers around selected methods, 100 warmed steps. It is instrumented and not throughput acceptance; stages are inclusive, so do not sum nested totals. The raw diagnostic covers forward only, not backward.
The first global-pool attribution prototype patches runtime callbacks; it is not production code or a complete-checkout benchmark.

Formal timings use complete imported main85, gate2/e778622 and immutable candidate snapshots, --lookup default; no runtime monkeypatch. 128 features, batch32, hotness4, D64/FP32/SGD; 20 warmups, six 100-step trials, five separately profiled calls.

Original affinity series: GPU1,2, both workers inherit CPUs4-11. GPU1 is NUMA0, GPU2 NUMA2, so rank1 is remote in that series. NUMA control uses rank0 CPUs4-7, rank1 CPUs36-39, before importing Torch; its process order differs and every sample is retained.

No other local GPU validation overlaps timing. External jobs share the machine and processes/trials vary. Changing affinity is an experimental control, not a code improvement or a reason to erase prior slower measurements.
TWRW tests use two/four local ranks with node-size2; four ranks emulate two nodes, not physical multi-node or NVLink/GIN validation.

Removing cache-copy reduction in independent negative snapshots produces wrong owner values on deepcopy and pickle failure. Those failures are intentional controls, not failures of the final production code.
